newsitem.title: UK: Middle East crude tankers steady, mood upbeat.
newsitem.headline: Middle East crude tankers steady, mood upbeat.

text.p: Crude tanker rates were mainly flat on Friday but with a fairly firm tone, brokers said.
"We're not seeing very much change all round," an Oslo broker said. "But business is not bad. We are quite optimistic about rates."

Very large crude carriers on Middle East-Japan voyages were little changed at W60-65, with several brokers commenting on a difference of about 10 points between fixtures using modern vessels to Japan and South Korea and Middle East-Singapore trips employing older ships.
"Japanese and Korean charterers have again led the way so far as competing for modern ships (is concerned)...The gap is widening," brokers Galbraith's said in a weekly report.
Mideast-west VLCCs were at a steady W55, with brokers noting greater demand for voyages east.

Transatlantic trips were pegged at around W62.5 for VLCCs to the U.S. Gulf, unchanged from Thursday, and at W67.5 to Canada. "Canada is more expensive because of weather delays at this time of year," one broker said.
Brokers said the West Africa-U.S. sector was brisk but rates were generally steady. However, they were slightly firmer for million-barrel ships, with up to W90 paid to USAC, up from W87.5.
In the inter-UKC sector, 80,000 tonne vessels were fixed mainly at around W105-107.5 but brokers said this could vary considerably, depending on dates.
"This has been going on for some days. There are very good rates and also some very bad rates. It all depends on dates," one added.
UKC fuel oil was one sector that has firmed sharply, with 25,000 tonnes up 20 points at W195.
"A number of (fuel oil) vessels have been cleaned up to take clean cargoes...The removal of just a few ships can boost the market by five or 10 points," one broker said.

He also said a number of fuel oil ships normally dedicated to short UKC trips had gone to the Med or the Canary Islands, taking them out of the sector for five to seven days, thus adding to the upward pressure.

Cross-Med 80,000 tonne vessels were fixed at an unchanged W105, with 130,000 tonnes likewise steady at W85-90. Despite lively business, there were enough vessels available to keep rates steady, brokers said.
Likewise, the busy Caribbean sector was little changed from Thursday with 70,000 tonners at W160 to USAC, but up about 10 points in a week. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
